content.text: Aozora Outfit Management System NG · Outfit saving, instant dressing, material customization, and character management
NG release line rebuilt from the post-2.0.4 system with a direct-commit model: selecting an outfit or changing an item in the studio immediately changes the character's worn outfit.
Save, equip, and edit outfits for the player and NPCs; closing the menu or studio keeps the character's current worn state.
Plugin files, MCM identifiers, and data folders retain the OutfitManager name for compatibility with existing settings and outfits.

content.help: Open or close Aozora Outfit Management System NG.
Open the Outfit Studio directly for the current target.
Equip the current target with a random saved outfit matching their gender.
Open the simple outfit selector; GOE chooses the target, or the player is used when no target is found.

content.text: Usage counts are stored in each outfit JSON file and are shared across save games.

content.help: Slot Order uses the original ascending slot order. Usage Frequency places frequently equipped outfits first and resolves ties by slot number.
Set every saved outfit's cross-save usage count to zero.

content.text: The studio edits the character's current worn outfit directly; equip, unequip, material, and exit actions keep the current real state.

content.help: Show the Outfit Studio entry on the main management page. Enabled by default.

content.text: When enabled, saved outfits include the equipped weapon, standard modifications, and legendary effects.
Applying an outfit creates a new independent weapon from the saved record instead of reusing one from inventory.
Recognizable unique or special Fallout4.esm modifications are filtered; standard modifications and legendary effects are retained.
Effects built into modded weapons, base records, scripts, or special data cannot be identified universally and may remain.
When the player or an NPC lacks the required ammo, the system silently supplies three magazines, from 30 to 180 rounds; each ammo type is supplied once per actor per save.
Switching outfits removes the last system-generated weapon. When disabled, the studio does not load weapons and only clothing is saved or equipped.

content.help: Save the equipped weapon, standard modifications, and legendary effects, then create a new independent weapon when applying the outfit. Disabled means the studio does not load weapons.

content.text: The preview uses three temporary world lights indoors and outdoors, with separate LIGH brightness scales. The slider uses fixed 0.25 steps: 0 disables compensation, followed by 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, and 200%. Indoor 100% matches the previously tested indoor 2.0 effect; changes apply on the next full preview open.

content.help: Adjust the indoor preview light from 0.0 to 2.0 in 0.25 steps. Each step selects a fixed LIGH record. Changes apply after closing and reopening the preview UI.
Adjust the outdoor preview light from 0.0 to 2.0 in 0.25 steps. Each step selects a fixed LIGH record. Changes apply after closing and reopening the preview UI.
Show status notifications for dressing and saving.
Show a required confirmation dialog after adding an outfit to a companion's inventory. Enabled by default.
Show a nudity warning before entering the studio. The studio always starts from the character's actual outfit. Disabled by default.
